 ## [Unreleased]
 
+## [0.20.1] - 2026-10-23
+
+A performance and diagnostics patch: rule path checks, nested-rule kinds and several other hot
+paths are cheaper, and alint now warns when a content pattern's `^` or `$` anchors to the whole
+file where a line was almost certainly meant (#343). Structured-query and cross-file checks run
+3-5% faster end to end, the docs explain what each kind matches a regex against, and releases
+gain a deterministic micro-benchmark gate and a long-horizon performance anchor.
+
+### Added
+
+- `xtask micro-det` counts the instructions of every criterion micro
+  benchmark under Callgrind, across git refs. Pull requests and pushes to
+  `main` run a curated low-noise subset (advisory); `bench-record` runs the
+  full suite at release and fails when a benchmark grows more than 3% over
+  the previous release.
+- A long-horizon performance anchor (`docs/benchmarks/ANCHOR`):
+  `xtask bench-gate --anchor` and `xtask micro-det --anchor` fail a release
+  that exceeds the anchor release by more than 10%, so creep that passes
+  every release-to-release check still surfaces. `bench-record` now runs
+  `bench-gate` itself and adds a same-session criterion A/B against the
+  previous release to the results PR.
+- **Warnings for mis-anchored content patterns.** In `file_content_forbidden`,
+  `file_content_matches`, `file_header`, `file_footer` and the
+  `file_content_matches` fact, `^` and `$` anchor to the whole file (or block),
+  so `^TODO` only ever checks line 1 and `TODO$` never matches a file that ends
+  in a newline (#343). alint now warns when a config loads with a `$` that
+  cannot match a newline-terminated file, or a forbidden pattern that starts
+  with `^`: on `check`, `fix`, `baseline`, `validate-config` (its JSON output
+  gains `warnings`) and as diagnostics on the config file in the editor. The
+  warnings never change findings or exit codes, and `--quiet` silences them.
+
+### Changed
+
+- The deterministic perf gate also runs on pushes to `main`, comparing the
+  pushed range.
+
+### Performance
+
+- **Every rule's path check is cheaper.** Matching a file against a rule's
+  `paths:` include and exclude globs prepared the path for matching twice, once
+  per glob set; it is now prepared once. The rule-dispatch benchmark drops 23%
+  in instructions and raw glob matching 12%.
+- **Nested-rule kinds are about three times cheaper.** `every_matching_has`,
+  `for_each_dir` and `for_each_file` build each nested rule once per matched
+  entry, and compiling its literal path (`packages/p0/README.md`) into a glob
+  set was most of that cost. A scope whose only pattern is a literal path now
+  matches by comparing the path instead. Nested rules also no longer re-run
+  build-time validation per entry, skip glob escaping for values with nothing
+  to escape, and derive only the path tokens their templates use. Instruction
+  counts drop 67-70% (`every_matching_has`, `for_each_dir`), below v0.17.0.
+- **`pair` and `unique_by` are cheaper.** Both now derive only the path tokens
+  their templates use; `pair` skips its partner-path normalization when the
+  rendered path is already normal, and `unique_by` groups keys in a hash map
+  (output order unchanged). Instruction counts drop 26-27% (`pair`) and 32-47%
+  (`unique_by`).
+- **Terminal output of many findings is cheaper.** The human, github and
+  markdown formats sanitize every path and message; printable ASCII now skips
+  the per-character check. Instruction counts drop 16-28%, below v0.17.0.
+- **YAML is scanned once, not twice, before parsing.** The denial-of-service
+  guards (flow-collection depth and alias expansion) share one pass and skip it
+  when the document has none of the bytes that could trip them. YAML structured
+  queries drop 16% (back to v0.17.0), `pinned_references` 22%.
+- **Loading an `extends:` chain is cheaper.** A config reached through
+  `extends:` is memoized only when it is loaded a second time (diamond chains
+  stay linear), and provenance markers are updated in place. A 16-level chain
+  loads with 21% fewer instructions.
+- **End to end**, against v0.20.0 on the bench host in two separate sessions,
+  structured-query and cross-file checks (S2, S4) run 3-5% faster from 10k to
+  1m files (best run of each cell). Walk- and content-scan-bound runs (S1, S3)
+  take the same time, although S1 now executes 6% fewer instructions.
+
+### Fixed
+
+- **What a content pattern matches against is documented.** A new "Regex
+  patterns and anchors" configuration page lists what each kind matches a
+  regex against and what `^` and `$` mean there, and the content rules'
+  reference pages and schema descriptions say how they anchor. Seven
+  mis-anchored patterns in the docs and case-study examples are corrected:
+  the monorepo page's `.bazelversion` shape check, for one, failed every
+  file that ends in a newline (#343).
+- The 1k `changed`-mode benchmark cells no longer swing between about 11
+  and 20 ms from one release to the next: the harness committed the
+  generated tree within one second, so git re-hashed every "racily clean"
+  file on each timed run. The index is now settled before timing.
+- The deterministic `det_engine` benchmark now counts the rayon worker that
+  evaluates rules; it had been counting about 0.06% of the engine's work.
+- Correct the crates.io Trusted Publishing instructions for a brand-new crate:
+  bootstrap its first tagged version with a scoped maintainer token from the
+  exact release commit, configure the crate's OIDC publisher, then rerun the
+  idempotent failed release job.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Summarize a same-session criterion A/B as Markdown.
+
+bench-record benches the previous release's criterion suite with
+`--save-baseline prev`, then the new ref's with `--baseline-lenient prev`.
+Criterion then writes `<bench>/change/estimates.json` (relative change of
+the mean and median, with a 95% confidence interval) for every benchmark
+both runs share. This prints one table row per benchmark, largest median
+change first, and marks a change "significant" when its confidence interval
+excludes zero. Report-only: nothing here gates.
+
+Usage: criterion-change-summary.py <criterion-dir> [--top N]
+"""
+import json
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def rows(root: Path):
+    for est in sorted(root.glob("**/change/estimates.json")):
+        bench_dir = est.parent.parent
+        meta = bench_dir / "new" / "benchmark.json"
+        try:
+            bench_id = json.loads(meta.read_text())["full_id"]
+        except (OSError, KeyError, ValueError):
+            bench_id = bench_dir.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+        data = json.loads(est.read_text())
+        median = data["median"]
+        lo = median["confidence_interval"]["lower_bound"]
+        hi = median["confidence_interval"]["upper_bound"]
+        yield bench_id, median["point_estimate"] * 100, lo * 100, hi * 100
+
+
+def main(argv):
+    if not argv or argv[0] in ("-h", "--help"):
+        print(__doc__.strip())
+        return 0 if argv else 2
+    root = Path(argv[0])
+    top = int(argv[argv.index("--top") + 1]) if "--top" in argv else None
+    found = sorted(rows(root), key=lambda r: -r[1])
+    if not found:
+        print("_No same-session comparison: the previous release's suite did not run._")
+        return 0
+    significant = [r for r in found if r[2] > 0 or r[3] < 0]
+    print(
+        f"{len(found)} benchmarks compared in one session; "
+        f"{len(significant)} with a significant median change (95% CI excludes 0).\n"
+    )
+    print("| Bench | Median change | 95% CI | |")
+    print("|---|---:|---:|---|")
+    shown = found if top is None else found[:top]
+    for bench_id, point, lo, hi in shown:
+        mark = "significant" if (lo > 0 or hi < 0) else ""
+        print(f"| `{bench_id}` | {point:+.2f}% | [{lo:+.2f}%, {hi:+.2f}%] | {mark} |")
+    if top is not None and len(found) > top:
+        print(f"\n{len(found) - top} more benchmark(s) not shown.")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Deterministic micro-bench gate, per-PR / per-push tier (advisory).
+#
+# `xtask micro-det` compiles the curated low-noise subset of the criterion micro
+# suite at HEAD and at the base (perf-gate-base.sh, the same base the
+# det-perf-gate.sh uses), runs each benchmark under Callgrind and compares
+# instructions per iteration. Load-immune, so it runs on any executor. A
+# regression past +3% annotates the run but never fails it; the full suite
+# gates releases in bench-record.yml. A gate that could not run fails the job,
+# labelled as tooling, so a blind gate never looks like a pass.
+set -uo pipefail
+cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" || exit 1
+
+summary() { printf '%s\n' "$@" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"; }
+tooling_failure() {
+  echo "::error title=Deterministic micro gate::$1 (tooling failure, not a perf signal); the gate did not run"
+  summary "### Deterministic micro benches: did not run" "" "Tooling failure: $1. See the job log."
+  exit 1
+}
+
+# shellcheck source=ci/scripts/perf-gate-base.sh
+source "$(dirname "$0")/perf-gate-base.sh"
+BASE_SHA="$(perf_gate_base)"
+HEAD_SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
+if [[ -z "$BASE_SHA" || "$BASE_SHA" == "$HEAD_SHA" ]]; then
+  echo "==> no distinct base to compare against — skipping"
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+if ! command -v valgrind >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  if ! { sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq valgrind; }; then
+    tooling_failure "could not install valgrind"
+  fi
+fi
+
+rows="$(mktemp)"
+trap 'rm -f "$rows"' EXIT
+workdir="${RUNNER_TEMP:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/micro-det"
+# Reuse the job's cached target dir for dependencies (micro-det cleans only the
+# workspace's own packages between refs).
+export CARGO_TARGET_DIR="${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$PWD/target}"
+echo "==> micro-det: ${BASE_SHA:0:12} -> ${HEAD_SHA:0:12} (pr subset)"
+if ! cargo run -q -p xtask -- micro-det \
+  --base "$BASE_SHA" --head "$HEAD_SHA" --suite pr --advisory \
+  --workdir "$workdir" --out-json "$rows" \
+  --summary "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"; then
+  tooling_failure "xtask micro-det did not complete"
+fi
+regressions="$(grep -cE '"verdict": "(regression|anchor_regression)"' "$rows" || true)"
+if [[ "$regressions" -gt 0 ]]; then
+  echo "::warning title=Deterministic micro gate::${regressions} micro bench(es) grew more than +3% in instructions (ADVISORY). See the job summary."
+fi
+echo "==> deterministic micro gate: done (${regressions} advisory regression(s))"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Print the commit a perf gate compares HEAD against (empty: nothing to compare).
+#   - pull request: PR_BASE_SHA, the PR's base;
+#   - push: PUSH_BEFORE_SHA, the tip before the push, so a direct push to main
+#     is gated on exactly what it changed. After a force-push the old tip is
+#     not an ancestor of HEAD; compare against where the histories meet;
+#   - otherwise: the merge base with origin/main.
+# Sourced by det-perf-gate.sh and micro-det-gate.sh so both gates agree.
+perf_gate_base() {
+  local before="${PUSH_BEFORE_SHA:-}"
+  if [[ -n "${PR_BASE_SHA:-}" ]]; then
+    printf '%s\n' "$PR_BASE_SHA"
+  elif [[ -n "$before" && "$before" != 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 ]] \
+    && git cat-file -e "${before}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
+    if git merge-base --is-ancestor "$before" HEAD 2>/dev/null; then
+      printf '%s\n' "$before"
+    else
+      git merge-base "$before" HEAD 2>/dev/null || true
+    fi
+  else
+    git merge-base HEAD origin/main 2>/dev/null || true
+  fi
+}

+**The 1k `changed` cells had a second, harness-made cause (found 2026-10).** Git, built
+without `USE_NSEC` (its default), treats a tracked file whose mtime falls in the same

+the second boundary fell: published 1k `changed` cells flipped between about 11 and
+about 20 ms from release to release with unchanged code (up to 43M extra instructions
+in git per run). `init_git_for_changed_mode` now waits out the second and lets `git

+### Mechanism
+
+`alint check --changed` runs `git ls-files --modified --others --exclude-standard`. Git (built without `USE_NSEC`, its default) treats any index entry whose mtime falls in the same wall-clock **second** as `.git/index` as *racily clean*: the stat data cannot prove the content unchanged, so `ie_match_stat` re-reads and re-hashes the file. `ls-files` never rewrites the index, so the same entries are re-hashed on every invocation, forever.
+
+The harness generates the 1k tree, then runs `git add -A` and `git commit` in roughly 0.2 to 0.3 s. Whether a second boundary falls inside that window is luck, so a run gets anywhere from none to all of the tree racy, and keeps that state for every timed sample.

+|---|---:|---:|---:|
+| 1 to 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
+| 5 | 1001 | 901 | 0 |
+| 6 | 717 | 638 | 0 |
+| 7 | 313 | 280 | 0 |
+| 8 | 372 | 331 | 0 |

+Re-reads equal the same-second count minus the touched 10% (those changed size, which git detects without reading). The files re-read have index stat data byte-identical to the filesystem; only the same-second rule triggers the read.

+### Changes from the proposal
+
+- **C1, re-scoped.** A compile-once nested plan would re-implement each child kind's evaluation. Profiling the B-phase build showed most of a nested entry's remaining cost was compiling the rendered literal path into a `GlobSet` (18.6k of 30.9k Ir per entry in `every_matching_has/1000`). `Scope::from_patterns` now recognizes a sole literal include pattern and matches it by byte comparison, which is globset's literal strategy. Where `\` is a separator (Windows), globset rewrites a pattern's `\` to `/` outside character classes, so the literal is normalized the same way and a pattern containing a class keeps the `GlobSet`. The first push missed this and failed `windows-latest`. An exhaustive test checks every pattern up to length 3 against a real `GlobSet` on every CI platform.
+- **Found during validation: one glob candidate per scope check.** The same-session criterion A/B showed `glob_match` +2 to +5% wall-clock with flat instruction counts. The single-literal branch had tipped LLVM's inliner: one of the two `GlobSet::is_match` calls in `Scope::matches` was no longer inlined into per-file loops. `is_match` prepares a fresh `Candidate` (normalization, basename, extension) on every call, so every check was preparing the path twice, even for an empty `exclude` set. One shared candidate with `is_match_candidate` removes that cost and the inlining sensitivity: `rule_engine` -23%, `glob_match` -12%, every other rule kind -2 to -4% (Ir).
+- **C2.** `PathTokens::from_path_with` derives only the tokens a template uses, and every token when the path needs glob escaping, so message unescaping is unchanged.
+- **C3.** `scan_guards` answers both YAML guards (flow depth and alias expansion) from one prefiltered lexer pass at all ten call sites. The expansion budget pass still runs only when an alias was seen.
+- **C4, declined.** `run_for_file` is +26% against v0.17.0, about 2.6k instructions per call (under a microsecond per LSP re-evaluation). Caching the gate would add an invalidation path for that saving.
+- **C5.** `unique_by` groups in a `HashMap` and sorts only the colliding keys, so report order is unchanged; a test pins it.
+- **C6, narrow.** Extends provenance and field-source markers are updated in place in one pass per mapping. Moving the marking into deserialization was not needed for the gain.
+- **1k `changed` cells stay advisory.** On kbench, 5 interleaved fresh trees per harness: S1 spread 79% → 12%, S2 65% → 12%, S4 7% → 2%. The bimodality is gone, but ±6 to 9% residual on a 10 to 20 ms cell is still too wide to gate.
